children: The FTSE 100 traded higher on Wednesday after falling 0.3% in the previous session, supported by continued weakness in oil prices and renewed hopes for progress in US-Iran diplomacy.
Oil prices extended their decline for a sixth consecutive session, putting Brent on track for its longest losing streak in more than a year.
Prices fell after President Donald Trump said US officials had held a “very good” meeting with Iranian envoys as Washington renewed efforts to end the conflict.
Among individual stocks, JD Sports rose almost 1% after maintaining its guidance, despite trimming its outlook last month amid weakness in the trainer market.
Diageo fell around 0.8% after appointing Joanne Wilson, currently CFO of WPP, as its new chief financial officer from 2027.
Meanwhile, Airtel Money confirmed plans for a London listing that could become the city’s largest IPO since 2021, providing a potential boost to a subdued market.
Investors are also awaiting the latest UK PMI data.

title: FTSE 100 Attempts Rebound
